items.headline: Colorado UPK quality rules phase in July 2026: class cap 20, ratio 1:10
items.summary: Tighter caps than today's 24 children and 1:12 ratio mean more staff per classroom and lower per-room revenue for Colorado operators like Ken Caryl.

items.headline: Colorado CCCAP and Early Intervention facing funding shortfalls
items.summary: State subsidy programs are short of money, with universal preschool flagged as potentially next — a risk to subsidy-linked enrollment revenue.

items.headline: Colorado delays 7% family copay cap from Aug 2026 to Aug 2028
items.summary: Two more years before copayments are capped at 7% of income, deferring a revenue constraint for Colorado providers.

items.headline: Childcare among the most actively consolidated sectors; PE playbooks scaling
items.summary: Private equity is running dental/derm-style roll-ups in a still mom-and-pop market — supportive of multiples and add-on pipeline for KEP.

items.headline: Center-based care holds ~63% share as demand outstrips supply in most metros
items.summary: Dual-income household growth keeps waitlists tight, supporting enrollment and pricing power at quality centers.
